title: Construction layer of the canonical finite tensor comparison
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, n≥0, and a scheme morphism f:X→Y with l invertible on X and Y, with the coefficient categories and operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and finite coefficient rings of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Restrict the prescribed K-flat tensor model to flat-term K-flat representatives [def-sfb-proetale-tensor-model]. Identify the ordinary ringed pullback with the intrinsic finite pullback by the unique comparison preserving the actual adjunction-unit sections. Define finitePullbackTensorConstruction to be the composite of the inverse derived realization, inverse source tensor-model comparison, the canonical pro-etale tensor comparison, the target tensor-model comparison, and the tensor of the two derived realizations. Package this same family into a natural isomorphism, with identical components. Retain the four coefficient-level comparison-family types. These are the existing constructions extracted into an importable layer; canonicalFinitePullbackTensor is their API alias, with no replacement functors or arbitrary comparison maps.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product, proof and final displayed total map); Tag 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution); Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor and the following symmetry paragraph); More on Algebra, Tag 0FNG (section-sign-rules, item-flip-tensor-product).

proof.text: For pullbackTensorIndependent use the first property of the given flat-term K-flat representative: at these universes the two K-flat predicates are definitionally equal.

For pullbackTensorFiniteRepresentative_existsUnique use ObjectProperty.ιOfLE to include flat-term K-flat complexes among all K-flat complexes, and whisker T.comparison with the product inclusion. Set the tensor field to S.tensor. The component equation is reflexive. For uniqueness eliminate the asserted tensor-functor equality, then use isomorphism and natural-transformation extensionality and the prescribed component equations.

For pullbackTensorFiniteRealization_existsUnique specialize openSquarePullbackModel_existsUnique to the finite coefficient ring at exponent n+1. The constant-ring identifications and the displayed adjunction-unit section equations agree definitionally.

Compose the five already specified natural isomorphisms to form finitePullbackTensorConstructionIso. Its component is definitionally the displayed finite comparison family. No additional existence theorem is used.
